reasons: Placeholder keys must be replaced before the paid examples work.
The cost estimate is typed in, not computed.
Most configuration steps are commented out by default.

terms.meaning: A free tool that runs open-source language models on your own computer.
The saved choice of which model handles which task, plus its settings.
A stand-in value that must be replaced with a real one before use.
The share of model calls that completed without an error.

depends_on: a local Ollama service for open-source setups

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Server address and imports
sections.what: Brings in the tools for web requests and JSON, and sets the server address to the local machine on port 8000.
sections.why: Likely reason: the example talks to a server running on this computer.
sections.watch_out: The server must be running before any call is made.

sections.name: initialize_model_registry
sections.title: Fill the model catalogue
sections.what: Asks the server to fill the catalogue with default models and prints the total number of entries.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed before browsing or recommendations on a fresh install.
sections.watch_out: Whether repeat calls add duplicate entries is not visible from this file.

sections.name: browse_available_models
sections.title: Show catalogue grouped by task
sections.what: Fetches all catalogue entries, groups them by task and by kind, and prints the top two of each group with quality, memory or cost.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the catalogue easy to scan.
sections.watch_out: The grouping depends on exact model kind names, and a task with no recommended list is skipped.

sections.name: get_task_recommendations
sections.title: Show best models for a task
sections.what: Asks the server for the best models for one task, planning by default, and prints open-source and paid options with quality, cost, speed and documentation link.
sections.why: Likely reason: helps the user pick models before configuring them.
sections.watch_out: The task name is placed in the web address, so it must match a real task name exactly.

sections.name: configure_open_source_workflow
sections.title: Set open-source models for all tasks
sections.what: Sends three setups for planning, generation and validation that use models hosted by a local Ollama service, and prints each result.
sections.why: Reason for the different temperature values is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Ollama must be running and the named models downloaded first. The 70 billion parameter model usually needs a lot of graphics memory, so check the catalogue figure.

sections.name: configure_paid_workflow
sections.title: Set paid models for all tasks
sections.what: Sends three setups using paid hosted models from two providers, with keys read from placeholder values, and prints each result.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the highest quality option. The specific model choices are not explained in the code.
sections.watch_out: Never save a real key in this file or share it, since it can be used to bill your account. The model names may be out of date, so check the catalogue.

sections.name: configure_mixed_workflow
sections.title: Mix paid and open-source models
sections.what: Sends one paid setup for planning, one open-source setup for generation and one paid setup for validation, then prints each result and a fixed cost estimate.
sections.why: The comments say each choice is made for quality, cost or speed.
sections.watch_out: The monthly cost estimate is typed into the message and is not calculated, so it may not match real use.

sections.name: view_current_configs
sections.title: List saved setups
sections.what: Fetches saved setups and prints each one with a default marker, model, kind, provider, call count, speed and success rate. Prints a message if none exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user check what was set up after a configure step.
sections.watch_out: Success rate is shown as a percentage, so a missing value would cause a printing error. The speed line is skipped when the value is empty or zero.

sections.name: test_configuration
sections.title: Run a test planning request
sections.what: Sends a small planning request and prints the model used, its response time and the number of sections.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the planning model works from start to finish.
sections.watch_out: Only planning is tested. Authoring, validation and publishing setups are not checked here.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Run the registry setup step
sections.what: When the file runs directly, only fills the catalogue and prints planning recommendations. All configuration and test steps are commented out.
sections.why: Likely reason: the user chooses a strategy by uncommenting one step.
sections.watch_out: Running the file as it is configures nothing, so a user may think setup is complete.

summary: A runnable script that shows how to browse models, set up open-source or paid models for each task, view the setups, and test planning.
purpose: Teaches a user how to choose and check the model used for each task.
why: Likely reason: the choice of model affects quality, cost and speed, so the example shows the trade-offs.
how: Calls the model routes to fill the catalogue, browse and recommend models, send configuration requests for each strategy, list saved setups, and send a test planning request. Only the first two calls run by default.
inputs: A server running at the local address, plus placeholder API keys that must be replaced by the user.
outputs: Printed lists of models, configuration results, saved setups and a test result.
risks: Placeholder keys must be replaced, and real keys must never be saved in this file. The model names may be out of date. The monthly cost estimate is a typed-in figure, not a calculation.
debug: If a call returns not found, check that the path includes the same version prefix the server uses. If setup fails, read the error text printed. If a paid model fails, check the key and the model name in the catalogue. If an open-source model fails, check that the local Ollama service is running and the model is downloaded.
